analysis:
Reviewed unit 0 and independently checked the replayed patches, file metadata, and documentation against the canonical definition index and selected boundary details. No supported security regression was identified.

.github/workflows/release-desktop.yml adds DMG signing before notarization (head line 142), then signature verification, expected-team enforcement, and an explicit Notarized Developer ID check (head lines 172–176). The visible shell uses set -euo pipefail, so failures in the new assessment/tee pipeline stop execution. Existing stapler and image-integrity checks remain in the patch context. These additions strengthen release artifact integrity relevant to T-013/T-034 without introducing a new endpoint or credential type.

docs/operations/desktop-release.md:57–58 accurately describes the new checks and preserves the separate real-hardware qualification limitation at 71–72. changelog.d/desktop-release-sign-dmg.md:3–5 describes the same change; its historical dry-run claim is not independently verified or relied upon. Container signing is not App Attest code qualification or serving permission (A-017, T-054, TB-011), and the documentation does not newly claim otherwise.

The supplied changes do not alter provider authorization, endpoint-key custody, inference encryption, plaintext handling, billing, cancellation, cache storage, or privileged helper behavior. Replay omits two workflow source units, so the prior analysis's detailed claims about credential selection, publication ordering, and cleanup were not independently revalidated. This limits coverage but does not establish a material unresolved vulnerability in the visible additive, fail-closed checks. Build internals, installer behavior, live Apple acceptance, and platform authorization remain outside the supplied source scope; this is not a full security audit or deployment qualification.
